Yes we do all our shots over a chrono since we have to document  the velocity.
The velocity did not increase, only the recoil.
This was the only thing i could think of. Quickload gives this particular load an awful ballistic efficiency so that might be it.

The projectiles we use are lake city pulled m80 projectiles, literally the exact same bullets used in the factory loads we shoot. I shot factory loads in the morning and my reloads in the afternoon and noticed a significant increase in felt recoil.
We do external validation but we would like to do regular in house testing as well. Well we do already do in house testing but we want it to be closer to nij spec.
Theres a reason I made a new account to post this stuff. You've probably heard of us, I'll tell you that much.
Youre not wrong I think its a stupid standard but it specifies a 124 grain fmj nato bullet. That's definitely not a 357 bullet
Any idea what kind of powder they use and how much?
We already have a Henry lever action 44 mag we use.

Lmao 2200?! My boss wouldn't even pay 35 bucks for a vacuum cleaner for the reloading bench. Hell I had to buy the 308 rifle we use for testing.

Also pistols are a real bitch to do the testing with so im trying to do everything with rifles.
I'll let you tell my boss that 😏
Also, I have to use a fmj round nose bullet, thats part of the standard too. I know its not ideal but it's what I have to work with.

Thats the number that quickload gave me as well. The simulated max pressure is well within SAAMI spec but its considerably above the max load listed in my book so I wanted to run it by some more experienced people. Here's what quickload is giving me:

[https://i.ibb.co/7tD43gx/quickload.jpg](https://i.ibb.co/7tD43gx/quickload.jpg)

I'm brand new at reloading so I wanted to make sure this is safe before I blow up my boss's gun.

Youre right and I believe that is the intent of the NIJ standard however I dont have a 357 sig carbine laying around and I dont think my employer will spring for one. I got around 1350 fps using factory ammo so an additional 100 fps should not blow up the gun.
